before.title: 48V Mild-Hybrid ISG / 48V Battery Malfunction Causing Sudden Power Loss
before.description: GLE models equipped with the EQ Boost 48-volt mild-hybrid system (GLE 350, GLE 450, GLE 450d, GLE 580 and AMG variants on the W167 platform) commonly trigger a '48V Battery Malfunction' or 'Hybrid System Error' warning. The integrated starter-generator (ISG) and 48V lithium-ion battery, along with the DC/DC converter, are known weak points. Owners report sudden loss of drive power on the motorway, disabled stop/start, weak acceleration and repeated stalling, sometimes resolving only after the car is powered down for 10-15 minutes. A March 2022 Mercedes TSB acknowledged that the battery self-test can disconnect the 48V battery due to software, hardware, cooling or false-positive faults. Many owners report multiple unsuccessful dealer visits and weeks of downtime, with the fault often persisting under warranty.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform Xentry diagnostics and apply the latest 48V/ISG control-unit software update first, as many cases are false-positive disconnects fixed in software. Persistent faults require replacement of the 48V battery, the integrated starter-generator (ISG/alternator unit), or the DC/DC converter. Check the 48V ground cable connection (subject of a separate recall) before condemning the battery. Repairs are typically covered under the powertrain/hybrid warranty; out of warranty an ISG replacement is a major job.

before.title: A/C Drain Hose Water Intrusion into Front Footwells (Recall 21V-288)
before.description: On 2020-2021 GLE and GLS SUVs, the air-conditioning condensation drain hoses can be incorrectly installed or disconnect during assembly, allowing condensate to drain into the driver and passenger front footwells instead of out under the vehicle. Owners report soaked carpets, fogged windows, a musty smell and standing water in the footwells. Beyond the nuisance, trapped water can corrode and short the floor-mounted electrical/control modules, which can disable the eCall emergency-call feature, prevent the doors from unlocking, and cause the engine to not start or enter limp-home mode. NHTSA recall campaign 21V-288 (an expansion of 19V-587) addressed this, with the recall later expanded again in 2023.
before.solution: Confirm the VIN against NHTSA recall 21V-288 / Mercedes campaign and have the dealer inspect and correctly route/secure the A/C drain hoses free of charge. Dry the carpet and underlay thoroughly and inspect floor-mounted control modules and connectors for corrosion; replace any water-damaged modules. Check that footwell drain paths are clear to prevent recurrence.

before.title: Diesel AdBlue / SCR NOx Sensor Fault Triggering Restart Countdown and No-Start

before.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Sudden Loss of Assist - "Power Steering Malfunction, See Operator's Manual"
before.description: GLE owners (W166 and W167) report sudden loss of electric power steering assist, sometimes immediately after engine start and sometimes intermittently while driving, accompanied by the red dashboard message "Power Steering Malfunction - See Operator's Manual." Steering becomes very heavy, especially at low/parking speeds. Because EPS relies on stable voltage, CAN/FlexRay communication, and accurate sensor data, causes are almost always electrical: EPS control-module/torque-sensor faults, a corroded/loose steering-rack ground or harness connection, a blown power-steering pre-fuse, or a weak 12V battery dropping voltage to the EPS motor. NHTSA recall 16V899000 covers 2016-2017 GLE (350/400/300d/550e/43/63, etc.) where an insufficiently sealed EPS connector lets water into the control unit and deactivates assist, and TSB MC-10231025 addresses a no-assist-after-start software fault of the N68 EPS control unit on later models. This is an electronic EPS-rack fault, separate from mechanical front control-arm bushing wear.
before.solution: Diagnose with XENTRY for C15xx EPS codes; first rule out and correct low battery voltage, a blown power-steering pre-fuse, and corroded/loose steering-rack ground and power connectors (common fixable causes). Check VIN for recall 16V899000 (connector reseal + rack inspection/replacement) and applicable EPS software TSBs. If the fault is internal, the EPS control unit / torque sensor or the complete electric steering rack is replaced (or reconditioned) and coded to the vehicle.
symptoms: "Power Steering Malfunction, See Operator's Manual" red warning message
Sudden heavy / hard-to-turn steering, worst at parking speeds
Intermittent loss and return of power assist after restart

before.title: M278 4.7L Twin-Turbo V8 (GLE 550) Timing Chain Tensioner / Camshaft Adjuster Cold-Start Rattle
before.description: The M278 4.7L biturbo V8 used in the GLE 550 4MATIC (W166/C292) has a complex timing drive with one primary chain and two secondary chains, each with its own tensioner. On early engines the secondary chain tensioners lose oil pressure during shutdown because they lack anti-drainback check valves, so on cold start the chains and camshaft adjusters run momentarily dry and rattle loudly for the first 2-5 seconds until oil pressure builds. Left unaddressed, chain slack, worn guide rails, and worn camshaft adjusters can advance to camshaft-correlation faults and, in the worst case, timing jump. This is distinct from the M276 V6 camshaft-adjuster rattle: it is the V8 M278's multi-chain oil-starvation design, and Mercedes issued a service fix (TSB LI05.10-P-056435) adding oil check valves plus revised secondary tensioners for engines up to a specific engine-number cutoff (278 9xx).
before.solution: Install the revised secondary timing chain tensioners together with the oil anti-drainback check valves in the cylinder-head oil passages per the Mercedes service procedure; inspect and replace worn chain guide rails and the camshaft adjuster (solenoid) units as needed. If the primary chain is stretched, a full timing chain/guide service is required. Verify no cam/crank correlation codes remain after repair.

before.title: OM651 Diesel Turbo Bearing Collapse and EGR Cooler Coolant Leak
before.description: The W166 GLE 250d and GLE 350d (2015-2019, OM651 2.1L twin-turbo / OM642-related diesels) have a documented pattern of turbocharger bearing collapse and EGR cooler failure, typically appearing between roughly 75,000 and 95,000 miles. On failure, replace the turbocharger and clear oil-feed/return lines of coking; severe bearing failures that ingest debris often require an engine rebuild or replacement. A leaking EGR cooler must be replaced and the cooling/oil system flushed. Coked injectors require cleaning or replacement and recoding.
